SEOUL: North Korea’s state media KCNA reported on Saturday (Oct 31) that the country’s defence science research institutes tested a major weapon system. The test was intended to “assess adaptation to combat and power of a cluster-bomb warhead to be tipped on tactical ballistic missiles”, KCNA said. The test found that a standard Type 2 cluster bomb warhead can destroy a target area of 12ha to 13ha at its highest density, KCNA said. The cluster bomb warheads fall into four categories, an official at North Korea’s missile administration said without elaborating.

North Korea will enable its military units by the end of 2026 to use all types of the bombs, depending on their operational purposes, KCNA said. Pyongyang has ramped up its show of force in recent weeks with multiple missile tests and holding a drone exhibition. Analysts said the tests could be part of efforts to modernise the military. North Korea gained experience in modern warfare, sending troops to the war in Ukraine for its ally Moscow. North Korea test-fired around 10 ballistic missiles from its east coast toward the sea on Oct 29, when German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited South Korea for a summit.

SEOUL, Nov 1 : South Korea's exports nearly doubled in October from a year earlier, beating market expectations and marking the sharpest jump in more than 50 years, trade data showed on Sunday. Exports from Asia's fourth-largest economy, a bellwether for global trade, rose 93.7 per cent last month to $115.28 billion, slightly higher than a median 93.2 per cent rise forecast in a Reuters poll of economists. The increase, boosted by favourable calendar effects of more working days due to the timing difference in local Chuseok holidays, beat September's 83.7 per cent gain and was the strongest since January 1974. Overseas sales of semiconductors jumped 259.4 per cent as prices and volume remained high on continued facility investment by global big tech firms in the competition for artificial intelligence industry leadership, the trade ministry said.

Oct 31 : Sovereignty won the Breeders' Cup Classic at Keeneland on Saturday, giving Venezuelan jockey Junior Alvarado and trainer Bill Mott a major victory after the colt was forced to miss last year's race through illness. The 4-year-old pulled away from the field to beat The Puma in the $7 million race, with stablemate Knightsbridge finishing third. Japan's Forever Young, which was seeking a second successive Classic victory, finished fifth. Sovereignty had been scratched from last year's race after developing a fever, despite entering as the 6-5 morning-line favourite. The colt had won the 2025 Kentucky Derby, Belmont Stakes and Travers Stakes before the scratch and was later named Horse of the Year. Racing behind pace-setting Knightsbridge for much of Saturday's 1-1/4-mile race, Sovereignty made its move turning for home and surged clear under Alvarado to complete the distance in 2 minutes and 0.36 seconds.

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Liam Lawson apologised to Max Verstappen on Saturday after the pair collided during practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix, saying the contact had not been intentional. The Racing Bulls driver said he had approached the four-times world champion that morning to clear the air after their clash in Friday's second practice session, which brought out a red flag and prompted a stewards' investigation. "I went to see Max this morning to apologise. Obviously, it was never my intention to make contact," Lawson told reporters after qualifying. "Obviously, for both of us, it's not good, so yeah, I'll learn from it going forward."

Verstappen had been critical of his former Red Bull team mate after the incident, questioning Lawson's judgement and suggesting it was particularly unwise given the New Zealander's uncertain future in Formula One. "Ultimately only Max knows how he feels," Lawson said. "Like I said, it was never my intention to have contact. So apologies for that." The stewards handed both drivers one-place grid penalties and a penalty point each, dropping Verstappen from fourth to fifth and Lawson from eighth to ninth on Sunday's starting grid. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton took pole position. With his 2027 future still uncertain, the 24-year-old Lawson said he was focused on making the most of his remaining opportunities. "Formula One is a tough sport, so I'm trying to do my best. I'm trying to score in every race that I can," he said.

FAST

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli said he had been driving with more tension than usual as the 20-year-old prepared for a Mexican Grand Prix that could make him Formula One's youngest world champion. The Italian is set to line up fourth on the grid at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday and needs only to finish ninth to secure the title, becoming Italy's first champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. "Definitely, I've been a bit more tense than usual, especially when you keep hearing, wherever you go, any time of the day, the same thing," Antonelli told reporters on Saturday. Antonelli, who was fifth fastest in qualifying but gained a place after Red Bull's Max Verstappen received a grid penalty, said the prospect of the title being treated as a formality had been difficult to ignore.

"People telling that it's already done," he said. "Knowing myself, I've been trying to block as much as possible this noise, but it hasn't been easy." Antonelli's closest title rival is Mercedes teammate George Russell, who qualified second, 123 points behind with only 100 remaining to be won after this weekend. Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who secured the pole position, must win on Sunday to delay Antonelli's coronation. ILLNESS PROBLEMS The championship leader has also been recovering from illness, having suffered a high fever and stomach problems on Thursday. "I still haven't recovered completely," Antonelli said, adding his energy levels were low and he had not been sleeping well. "It's not an excuse, but for sure it hasn't been my finest (drive)." Antonelli said he felt competitive in the second phase of qualifying on used tyres but struggled to produce a clean lap on fresh rubber in the final shootout. His starting position nevertheless gives him a strong opportunity to secure the points he needs, although Turn One in Mexico City can create a chaotic opening lap. "It's going to be important to get off the line well," he said. "Turn One is always very tricky. But I think if we get a good start, we have a good chance to move forward." Antonelli said he would try to rest before Sunday, with his family having arrived in Mexico City. "Just going to try to disconnect as much as possible, good sleep, and then ready for tomorrow," he added.

Source: Reuters

FAST

RIYADH, Oct 31 : Twenty-one years, hundreds of millions of dollars and a place among boxing's all-time greats have done nothing to dim Saul "Canelo" Alvarez's hunger. For all the riches and glory, the Mexican still finds his greatest joy within the unforgiving confines of a 25-square-metre ring, where he reclaimed the world title on Saturday with a unanimous points win over Christian Mbilli. The bout went ahead in Riyadh after a week in which the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Iran-aligned Houthi missiles and drones aimed at the capital. Security concerns led to the cancellation or postponement of several Saudi events, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition. The 36-year-old Alvarez, returning to the ring for the first time in more than a year, relied on his trademark counter-punching and precise body shots to overcome the French champion and re-establish himself among boxing's elite.

The judges scored the fight 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110. "It’s something unbelievable. It feels like my first title. Now, after 21 years as a professional, 16 years ago I won my first title. Now I won that title again. I’m so proud of my team," Canelo said. "I love boxing. That's why I'm here, because I still love boxing and I enjoy it a lot." RELENTLESS PRESSURE Mbilli, who entered the contest with a record of 29 wins and one draw, looked to unsettle the Mexican with his relentless pressure and higher punch volume, but Alvarez landed the cleaner blows, including a sharp uppercut that made his opponent stagger in the seventh round. The victory marked a significant comeback for Alvarez, who suffered only the third defeat of his professional career when American Terence Crawford outpointed him by unanimous decision in September 2025. That loss cost Alvarez his undisputed super-middleweight crown, ending his reign as holder of the division's four major titles. Mbilli, 31, had been elevated to full WBC champion after Crawford's departure from the division, having previously held the interim title. The Cameroon-born boxer had fought to a split draw against Lester Martinez on the undercard of the Alvarez-Crawford showdown, ending a run of 29 consecutive professional victories. Saturday's result improved Alvarez's record to 64 wins, three defeats and two draws and handed Mbilli the first loss of his professional career. (Writing by Julien Pretot; Editing by Ken Ferris and Ed Osmond)

HANOI, Oct 31 : Vietnam will cut its average retail electricity price by 2 per cent and remove its special consumption tax on gasoline from November 1 to support economic stability and reduce costs for households and businesses, the government said on Saturday. • The average retail tariff will fall to 2,159.9 dong ($0.085) per kilowatt-hour, excluding value-added tax, the government said in a statement • Its special consumption tax on gasoline will be cut to zero from 7 per cent-10 per cent from November 1 until the end of March next year • The decision was intended to help maintain macroeconomic stability while supporting social welfare and business activity, it said • Vietnam targets an economic growth of above 10 per cent this year, and fourth-quarter growth must be higher than 12.5 per cent to meet that target

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Lewis Hamilton took his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Saturday with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli fourth on the grid for a ground-breaking race likely to make the 20-year-old Formula One's youngest champion. Antonelli needs only a ninth-place finish at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday to become Italy's first champion since 1953. He was fifth fastest in qualifying, when he admitted he felt tense, but will move up a place due to Red Bull's Max Verstappen, in fourth, taking a grid drop. The pole, in a time of one minute 16.514 seconds, was a record-extending 105th of Hamilton's stellar career. While he has had two sprint poles since he joined Ferrari last year, he has not had one at a regular grand prix since Hungary in July 2023 when he was at Mercedes - a wait of 1,197 days. "Thank you so much, it has been such a long time coming," Hamilton said over the team radio. "Mega job, guys - I am so grateful for the hard work you guys put in."

OLDEST POLE SITTER SINCE 1982 The pole also made the seven-times world champion, 41, the oldest pole sitter since American Mario Andretti, at 42, at Monza in Italy in 1982. Mercedes' George Russell, Antonelli's closest rival but 123 points behind his teammate with only 100 to be won after this weekend, was second fastest - just 0.009 adrift after taking provisional pole only for Hamilton to beat his time - and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc third and 0.119 off the pace. Both Hamilton and Russell have to win if either of the remaining contenders is to keep Antonelli waiting another week for the inevitable. "I struggled to get a good feeling from the tyres in Q3. I just didn't have the most confidence. I was a bit tense, I am not going to lie," the Italian said. "It was a poor lap, too many mistakes. "It has not been the easiest weekend. There is talk of what is there and I am not as relaxed." McLaren's Lando Norris, the reigning champion and last year's winner in Mexico, qualified sixth with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar seventh. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson was eighth fastest but also has a one-place grid drop for the clash with Verstappen in Friday practice. That will mean the New Zealander starts ninth with teammate Arvid Lindblad eighth and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completing the top 10 on the grid. "I went to see Max this morning to apologise because what happened doesn't need to happen and I don't want it to happen in future," said Lawson.  The top 10 were separated by a mere seven tenths of a second. PIASTRI FAILS TO MAKE TOP 10 Antonelli was only seventh in the second phase, with Norris fastest and teammate Oscar Piastri knocked out in 13th place in a blow for McLaren's hopes of edging back in front of Red Bull in the battle for third overall. The Australian complained of lack of rear grip after being told he was out of the top 10. Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso halted the first session when the team told him to stop in the stadium section with a suspected water pressure issue in the power unit. The Spaniard was then noted for a general safety incident after he failed to reattach the steering wheel after getting out of the car. Hamilton was fastest in that first session, with Antonelli only ninth. Japanese Ryo Hirakawa, making his F1 race debut this weekend at the age of 32 and in place of Esteban Ocon who was dropped by the team for undisclosed reasons not related to illness, qualified 19th for Haas. Mexican Sergio Perez, preparing for his 300th grand prix in front of his home crowd, and Cadillac teammate Valtteri Bottas filled the back row.

Source: Reuters

MILAN, Oct 31 : AC Milan's Diego Moreira claimed one goal and two assists as his side took local bragging rights and three precious points with a 3-1 victory over Inter Milan in their Serie A clash on Saturday, while AS Roma enjoyed a 5-2 victory at Udinese. In a week when Milan and Inter announced they would build a new shared 71,500-seater stadium to replace the San Siro, Milan’s fast start earned the win that lifts them into fourth place, four points behind leaders Lazio and Inter who have 25. The result means Lazio can move three points clear of Inter when they host Cagliari on Sunday. Roma are third on 24 points. Milan made the perfect start as Christian Pulisic headed their opener after four minutes before Adrien Rabiot added a second six minutes later. Inter pulled a goal back through Alessandro Bastoni in the 22nd and the momentum was with them.

The next goal was always going to be crucial and it went to Milan as Moreira scored with a superb free-kick just before halftime to help his side to a fourth straight win over Inter. Roma were 4-0 up in 37 minutes at Udinese as they overwhelmed the hosts, who are second-bottom on five points. Bryan Cristante headed the first goal after 10 minutes, before Matias Soule and Donyell Malen struck the woodwork. Rodrigo Mora netted the second in the 31st minute after being set up by Cristante, and two minutes later Malen scored his eighth Serie A goal of the season. Evan Ndicka headed the fourth from a corner before halftime after which Udinese mounted something of a comeback. Nicolo Zaniolo and Matteo Palma scored for the hosts but Daniele Ghilardi added a fifth, his first Serie A goal, for Roma. "If we play like this there is a chance," Cristante said. "The league is not easy and it's nice to stay in (the title race). We are scoring a lot and that is very important," . Bologna climbed to ninth with a third successive league win thanks to a 2-1 victory over Monza, their first home success since April. Tommaso Pobega and Federico Bernardeschi netted for Bologna, after the visitors converted an early penalty through Gustavo Varela, the top Serie A scorer with nine goals in as many games. He had been substituted by the time Monza were awarded a second penalty in the final 10 minutes and this time Patrick Cutrone missed from the spot as they were denied a point.

Source: Reuters

Oct 31 : Barcelona enjoyed an emphatic 6-1 home win over Alaves on Saturday, with Raphinha, Fermin Lopez, Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon all on the scoresheet, as the hosts responded after losses to Real Madrid and Paris St Germain. Barca top LaLiga on 30 points, two ahead of Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0 earlier on Saturday, with Real Madrid six points off the pace before visiting Racing Santander on Sunday. The opening exchanges at Camp Nou were punctuated by frustrated shouts from home manager Hansi Flick in response to Barcelona's defending, but Alaves found it impossible to live with their fluid attacking play. After Pedri's pass sliced through the Alaves midfield, Fermin crossed for Raphinha to open the scoring in the eighth minute.

A brief Alaves reaction put the hosts under pressure but once Fermin netted from a tight angle in the 23rd minute, the game was one-way traffic in Barcelona's favour. Tenacious and incisive throughout, Fermin assisted Raphinha again in the 41st minute after winning possession back. Lamine rifled a bouncing ball low into the corner to complete a slick passing move, adding Barcelona's fourth in first-half stoppage time. Flick's side continued to look sharp and Karim Adeyemi spurned a chance to round off more excellent work from Fermin early in the second half. Lamine was set up by substitute Gabriel Jesus for his second in the 64th minute. Rodri was visibly delighted with the weight of his pass behind the Alaves defence, which Gordon converted for Barcelona's sixth with nine minutes remaining. The Spain midfielder was equally furious with himself after his giveaway allowed Mariano Diaz to add a consolation goal for Alaves three minutes later. "This is what I want to see after two defeats. How we reacted, it was good and in the right way," Flick said. MISSING VERVE Barca showed the verve they were missing in the 2-1 Clasico defeat by visitors Real, after which Flick said his team lacked freshness, and a 4-2 loss at PSG in the Champions League. Aston Villa visit the Catalan side on Tuesday in the Champions League in what is likely to be a sterner test. Midfielders Brian Farinas and Frenkie de Jong started in defence for Barcelona due to injuries, and Flick did not confirm when Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen or Eric Garcia would return. "We have to survive these two games (before the international break). We don't know who is coming back," said Flick. Diego Simeone won his 344th match as Atletico Madrid manager in a victory over Levante, equalling Luis Aragones' record in 192 fewer games. Goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone in each half were enough to secure a seventh straight victory in domestic competition. Fourth-placed Real Betis are revelling in their best start to a LaLiga season through 11 games since 1934, following a 2-1 win over Malaga. Rayo Vallecano moved level on 12 points with Celta Vigo after beating the Galician side 3-0, despite having played a game less.
